newsitem.title: USA: Dollar's rise worries US manufacturing group chief.
newsitem.headline: Dollar's rise worries US manufacturing group chief.

text.p: The head of the National Association of Manufacturers (NAM) voiced concern on Tuesday about the dollar's relentless rise and said his group planned to take up the issue with the Clinton administration soon.

"We're increasingly worried that the dollar appreciation is going to reduce export growth, will cut back on earnings for some companies and could get worse if it escalates higher," NAM President Jerry Jasinowski told Reuters.
"We will be taking this up with the administration and suggesting that it's an increasing problem and that we ought not to do anything to make the problem worse," he added.
"There's not much sign that there's any levelling off in store for us in the near term," Jasinowski added.

He said that both interest rate differentials between major nations and the currency policies of Japan and Germany point to the fact that "there's not much relief in sight" from the pressure of the strong dollar.

"The big problem appears to be that the Japanese and some Europeans are interested in trying to maintain low currencies in order to export their problems," he said. "That's what has us concerned more than anything else."
"We're trying to get a better understanding of what are the causes, consequences and possible things that can be done in order for the problem not to get any worse," he added.
